---

## 0. Design goals & threat model

- Property: For fixed genesis G and committed sequence of blocks, ANY conforming implementation computes identical 32-byte ledger root R_h for every height h. Tamper = any alteration of history ⇒ root mismatch detectable by replay or by proofs.
- Consensus: swarm of sovereign validators, rotating flock leader, Tendermint-style PBFT with QC chains; safety under n ≥ 3f+1 partially synchronous.
- Everything in the root path is a total, pure function of bytes. Time, randomness, iteration order, locale never touch it.

## 1. Primitives (pinned, no agility)

- Hash: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4). Output 32 bytes. Digests compared constant-time, rendered lowercase hex when logged.
- Signature: Ed25519 per RFC 8032 (deterministic signing). Keys are 32-byte pubkeys; sigs 64 bytes. (Optional BLS aggregation deferred to version 2 tag strings; V1 uses signature lists so QC bytes stay deterministic without pairing-order subtleties.)
- Integers: unsigned only, fixed width (u8/u16/u32/u64), little-endian on wire. No floats anywhere. Checked arithmetic; overflow ⇒ invalid input, never wrapping.
- Strings: none, except lowercase hex in human logs (never hashed). Identifiers are bytes.

Domain separation tags: 16-byte ASCII constants:

| Tag | Bytes | Use |
|---|---|---|
| TAG_GENESIS | "LEDGER-GENESIS\0\0" | genesis root |
| TAG_LEAF | "ENTRY-LEAF-----" | entry leaf hash |
| TAG_NODE | "TREE-NODE------" | internal tree node |
| TAG_HEADER | "BLOCK-HEADER---" | block hash |
| TAG_ROOT | "LEDGER-ROOT----" | chained ledger root |
| TAG_VOTE | "FLOCK-VOTE-----" | votes |
| TAG_QC | "QUORUM-CERT----" | QC binding |
| TAG_EPOCH | "EPOCH-BEACON---" | leader beacon |

Each exactly 16 bytes — pad/truncate names to fit. Let me count: "LEDGER-GENESIS" is 14 chars + 2 nulls = 16 ✓. "ENTRY-LEAF" 10 + 6 dashes = 16 ✓. "TREE-NODE" 9+7=16 ✓. "BLOCK-HEADER" 12+4=16 ✓. "LEDGER-ROOT" 11+5=16 ✓. "FLOCK-VOTE" 10+6=16 ✓. "QUORUM-CERT" 11+5=16 ✓. "EPOCH-BEACON" 12+4=16 ✓. 

Hash helper: H(tag, parts...) = SHA256(tag || part_1 || part_2 ...) where each variable-length part is prefixed with its u64 byte length. Rule: **every variable-length blob inside any hash input is length-prefixed with u64 LE**; fixed-width fields are raw. This kills ambiguity forever.

Wait — for Merkle tree nodes RFC 6962 uses 0x00/0x01 single-byte prefixes; I'll adapt: leaf = H(TAG_LEAF, entry_bytes) where TAG_LEAF plays role of 0x00 prefix (but stronger), node = H(TAG_NODE, left32 || right32) — fixed 64-byte concatenation, no length prefixes needed since fixed. Keep RFC 6962 tree *shape* but our own tags. Fine — call it "RFC 6962-shaped tree, domain-separated."

## 2. Canonical encoding

One encoder used for every struct that gets hashed or signed:

- Fields serialized in declaration order (the order in §tables below). No field may be omitted; no optional fields; no defaults.
- Variable-length: u64 LE byte-length prefix then bytes.
- Arrays: u64 LE element count then elements back-to-back.
- Enums: u16 LE, closed registry; decoder rejects unknown codes.
- No maps; key-value data encoded as array of (key: 32 bytes, value: blob) sorted by key ascending, duplicates rejected.
- Decoder is strict: trailing bytes ⇒ invalid; canonical integer encodings guaranteed by fixed widths (no varints).

This makes encode(decode(x)) == x and decode(encode(s)) unique — the two properties implementations need to match.

## 3. Data model

Entry (application record):
```
Entry {
  u16        version        = 1
  u32        stream_id      // logical log namespace
  u64        stream_seq     // per-stream strictly increasing, gapless
  bytes[32]  prev_root      // ledger root this entry extends (must equal current root at apply time)
  bytes      payload        // opaque, ≤ 1 MiB
}
```
Validity of entry E applied to state with root R: E.prev_root == R, stream_seq == next[stream_id]. Apply sets next[stream_id]+=1. Deterministic.

Block:
```
BlockHeader {
  u16        version = 1
  u64        height              // genesis=0, first block=1
  bytes[32]  prev_ledger_root    // R_{h-1}
  bytes[32]  body_root           // RFC6962-shaped root over entry leaves
  bytes[32]  parent_block_hash   // H(TAG_HEADER, header_{h-1}); 0^32 at h=1
  u64        epoch
  u64        round
  bytes[32]  proposer            // ed25519 pubkey of flock leader for (epoch,round)
  bytes[32]  epoch_seed          // beacon output committed by epoch's first block
  QC         parent_qc           // QC over parent block (height-1) — carries finality
}
BlockBody {
  u32        entry_count
  Entry[]    entries             // in sequencer order; order is consensus-relevant
}
Block = header ++ body; block_hash = H(TAG_HEADER, canonical(header))
```
Note body_root covers entries; block_hash covers header incl. body_root ⇒ commits body. prev_ledger_root in header makes each block commit to the entire prior ledger state root — the "every entry commits to prior root" requirement at both granularities (entry.prev_root intra-block, header.prev_ledger_root cross-block).

Hmm wait: entry.prev_root — if a block has multiple entries, entries 2..k have prev_root = root mid-block? Mid-block roots aren't committed until block finalizes. Options: (a) entry.prev_root always equals R_{h-1} for all entries in block h (they all extend the last finalized root); the running intra-block root R^partial_i = H(TAG_ROOT, R_{h-1}, leaf_i) is computed during apply but only R_h becomes durable. That's simplest and satisfies "every entry commits to the prior root": each entry's hash binds prev_root=R_{h-1}; the ledger root after the whole block folds all leaves. Go with (a): all entries in block h carry prev_root = R_{h-1}. Validation enforces equality. Clean.

Then define:
R_h = H(TAG_ROOT, R_{h-1} [32B] , body_root_h [32B], block_hash_h [32B])

Actually simpler and sufficient: R_h = H(TAG_ROOT, R_{h-1}, block_hash_h). Since block_hash already commits body_root and thus all entries. Including body_root separately is redundant; drop it from the root fold to minimize surface: R_h = H(TAG_ROOT, u64le(height), R_{h-1}, block_hash_h). Include height to prevent root reuse across parallel universes with same hashes (paranoia, cheap). Good.

Genesis: R_0 = H(TAG_GENESIS, canonical(GenesisDoc)).

```
GenesisDoc {
  u16       version = 1
  u32       chain_id         // 4-byte chain identifier, e.g., ASCII
  u32       initial_epoch
  u32       validator_count
  Val[]     validators       // sorted: stake desc, pubkey asc
  u64       max_entries_per_block = 8192
  u64       max_payload = 1048576
}
Val { bytes[32] pubkey; u64 stake; }
```
Validator ordering rule: primary key stake descending; secondary pubkey ascending (bytewise). Total order, no ties possible (pubkeys unique). Leader rotation uses THIS order — everyone derives it locally from genesis/epoch updates; never transmitted.

Epoch transitions: EpochChange entry type? Keep minimal: an epoch is 10,000 heights (fixed constant in genesis: u64 epoch_len). New epoch_seed = H(TAG_EPOCH, prev_epoch_seed, u64le(epoch)) — pure function; committed implicitly. Validators can rotate via governance entries — but governance adds surface; for V1: validator set fixed at genesis, epoch_len fixed. Note extension path: validator-set updates via special entry kind validated against current set, taking effect at epoch boundary k+2 (two-epoch delay), with new set sorted by same rule and hashed into epoch_seed: epoch_seed_e = H(TAG_EPOCH, seed_{e-1}, u64le(e), set_root_e). Mention briefly; V1 ships static set.

## 4. Merkle tree (body_root)

Exactly RFC 6962 shape, with our tags:

leaf(i) = H(TAG_LEAF, entry_bytes_i)
node(a,b) = H(TAG_NODE, a || b)

MTH over D[n]:
- n=0: SHA256() — the empty-string digest. Define body_root of empty block = SHA256("") = e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855. That hex I know cold (empty SHA-256) — correct.
- n=1: leaf(D0)
- n>1: k = largest power of two < n; MTH = node(MTH(D[0:k]), MTH(D[k:n]))

Recursion depth ≤ 13 for 8192 entries. Iterative formulation for implementers (same result): standard RFC 6962 algorithm — provide pseudocode both ways and assert equality.

## 5. Swarm consensus ("sovereign flock")

Roles: every validator gossips; leadership rotates per round ("flock leader"); sovereignty = any validator may propose if leader absent (view change), but only deterministic rules decide what counts.

Steps per (epoch e, height h, round r): PROPOSE → PREVOTE → PRECOMMIT, Tendermint-style, timeouts are liveness-only (values are local clocks; never enter hashes except proposer-provided block fields which are signed by all voters, hence agreed).

Leader: L(e,h,r) = VALIDATORS[ u32le_beacon mod n ] where beacon = first 8 bytes LE of H(TAG_EPOCH, epoch_seed_e, u64le(h), u64le(r)). Height-independent? Include h so leaders differ per height — fine, deterministic. Actually typical: leader per round regardless of height; but including h is harmless and more churn-resistant. Keep (h,r).

Proposal message P(h,r): Block B (full bytes) + valid parent_qc + optionally LastCommitQC. Signed by proposer. Valid iff:
- B.height == h; B.parent_qc verifies and certifies block at h-1 whose hash == B.parent_block_hash; B.prev_ledger_root == R stored for h-1 (node-local, but equal across honest nodes by induction);
- proposer == L(e,h,r);
- body constraints (count/payload limits, entry validity vs local R_{h-1});
- B.epoch == e.

Prevote(v) by validator v for block_hash X (or nil): signs H(TAG_VOTE, u16le(step=PREVOTE), u64le(h), u64le(r), X[32]). Rule: vote for proposed block if valid and proposer was leader; else nil. (Simplified Tendermint; locking discipline below preserves safety.)

Precommit similarly with step=PRECOMMIT.

QC(h, r, step, X): { u16 step, u64 h, u64 r, bytes32 X, u32 sig_count, Vec<(bytes32 pubkey, bytes[64] sig)> } with pubkeys sorted ascending, each sig verifying over the exact vote-hash above, sig_count ≥ 2f+1. QC hash = H(TAG_QC, canonical(qc_without_sigs) || concat(sig_list))? Careful: QC identity should be determined by (h,r,step,X) + member set; two QCs with different overlapping member subsets certify the same thing. For determinism of *referenced bytes*, we never need QC hash in the root — QCs appear in headers though! parent_qc bytes are inside header ⇒ block_hash depends on exact QC member subset chosen by proposer. Is that a problem for byte-identity? No: the full block bytes (incl. QC) are what 2f+1 sign; whatever subset the proposer picked becomes canonical once committed. Different proposers might pick different subsets, but only one block commits per height. ✓. Still, constrain: proposer MUST include ALL valid precommits it holds for (h-1, r', X) received before proposing — determinism of *content policy* helps storage dedup but isn't required for safety; state as MUST for tidiness, noting safety doesn't depend on it.

Commit rule (finality): Block B_h is FINAL when there exists QC_PRECOMMIT(h, r, B_h.hash) and a later block B_{h+1} whose parent_qc is exactly that QC (i.e., B_{h+1}.parent_block_hash == B_h.hash and parent_qc certifies it). Equivalently two-chain rule. Nodes persist R_h upon observing this. Also: any block at height ≤ h_final with hash ≠ committed ⇒ fatal halt (never rewrite).

Locking (safety sketch, keep terse): on sending precommit for X at (h,r), validator locks on (h,X). It prevotes only X at heights >h unless it sees a valid PRECOMMIT QC at some round r'' > r for different Y at same height, in which case it unlocks/switches. Standard Tendermint argument ⇒ no two values finalize at one height under n≥3f+1. One paragraph, cite mechanism, move on.

Timeouts/view-change: round increments on timeout; new leader per formula; proposals at higher rounds must carry the highest-round PRECOMMIT QC they know (LastCommit) so locked validators can verify justification — include field `just_qc` optional? No optionals! Make proposal always carry `parent_qc` (for h-1) AND `locked_qc` (precommit QC justifying proposer's right to propose at round r when r>0; at r=0 it's the zero-QC: step=0, X=0^32, sig_count=0). Zero-QC is canonical. Validation: if r>0 and proposer not... hmm, actually any locked validator can propose on timeout in Tendermint; here leader proposes; leader must respect others' locks by carrying justified QC. Simplify: proposals at round r>0 must include `highest_precommit_qc` known to proposer; validators accept proposal only if its height/round ≥ their lock round or QC justifies override (standard). This is the fiddliest part of PBFT; keep the spec statement tight and lean on Tendermint correctness rather than reinventing. The answer should show the rule precisely enough to implement: I'll define lock/unlock exactly:
